Wait, but maybe I'm missing something. Let me reconsider the movement rules.
In levels 1 and 2, the player moved 6 columns per step. But in level 3, maybe the player moves differently.
Actually, looking at the row 30 positions: 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36, 39, 42, 45, 48. The gaps are 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3. So the positions are every 3 columns.
But the player moves 6 columns at a time on row 30. From (30, 42), LEFT goes to (30, 36). From (30, 36), LEFT goes to (30, 30). From (30, 30), LEFT goes to (30, 24).
But going LEFT from (30, 36) to (30, 30) dies. So the player can't go past (30, 36).
Hmm, but what if the player moves 3 columns at a time on row 30? From (30, 42), LEFT goes to (30, 39). From (30, 39), LEFT goes to (30, 36). From (30, 36), LEFT goes to (30, 33). From (30, 33), LEFT goes to (30, 30).
But I tried LEFT from (30, 42) and the player went to (30, 36), not (30, 39). So the player moves 6 columns at a time on row 30.
OK so I'm really stuck. Let me try going UP from (36, 30) to (30, 30) one more time, but this time I'll check the animation to see exactly where the player dies.
Actually, I already know that going UP from (36, 30) to (30, 30) dies. So let me not waste another action on that.
Wait, actually I never tried going UP from (36, 30) to (30, 30). I tried going LEFT from (30, 36) to (30, 30), which died. And I tried going LEFT from (30, 30) to (30, 24), which also died (because the player was already dead).
Let me try going UP from (36, 30) to (30, 30) and see what happens. Maybe the player survives when going UP from (36, 30) to (30, 30), but dies when going LEFT from (30, 36) to (30, 30).
Actually, this is a good hypothesis. The collision model might be different for horizontal and vertical movements. When the player moves horizontally, the player's body sweeps across columns, which might overlap with B blocks. When the player moves vertically, the player's body sweeps across rows, which might not overlap with B blocks.
Let me try going UP from (36, 30) to (30, 30).
